data.title: What Avnet Holders Got Right
data.description:

That outcome naturally raises a tougher question. Back on 6 November 2025, what could have helped you see more than a cyclical bounce and focus instead on the specific claim that IoT, AI and electrification would reshape where this distributor earns its future margins?

The Two Avnet Stories Investors Had To Weigh

The shares cost US$47.17 at the start of the period, and Avnet sat between two very different stories about what came next.

The bullish view argued that IoT, AI and electrification would open higher quality business for Avnet, with a Fair Value of US$64, a price implied by assumptions that Farnell could return to double digit operating margins within 4 to 8 quarters.

The bearish camp saw direct supply chains and digital rivals eroding that upside, with a Fair Value of US$43 and a key worry that large manufacturers might increasingly bypass distributors and squeeze long term margins.

What The Results Told Investors About Avnet’s Story

Record quarters tied to AI and data center demand, plus Farnell reaching its strongest operating margin in three years, leaned toward the optimistic Avnet case that higher quality electronics work could lift profitability. The useful takeaway is how much the thesis hinged on margins, not headlines. For any distributor, track segment operating margins and net margin side by side with IoT or AI claims before deciding how much of the story to believe.

data.title: Missed Sartorius's Rally? What Holders Had To Believe
data.description:
If Sartorius was on your watchlist rather than in your portfolio, the past year may feel like a missed shot. For Sartorius shareholders, the return over the past year was 31.1%, including dividends. That outcome invites a harder question. Back on 6 November 2025, when bullish analysts argued that cell and gene therapies would expand bioproduction demand, what clues, if any, pointed to that secular bet being more than just an optimistic story?

Sartorius is not the only name tied to this theme. Zero in on 126 healthcare AI stocks and compare how each one is priced.

The Two Stories Sartorius Investors Had To Weigh

The shares cost €223 at the start of the period, and Sartorius sat between two very different but plausible stories about its future.

The bullish narrative argued that expanding cell and gene therapies, together with the shift away from animal testing, would support a Fair Value of €310. This price level was implied by assumptions of 10.9% annual revenue growth and profit margins rising from 3.0% to 11.8% by 2028.

The bearish view pointed to tariffs, regulatory pressure and lower cost rivals, backing a Fair Value of €175. This scenario assumed slower 6.6% revenue growth with margins reaching only 7.5% despite higher earnings.

What The Results Changed For The Sartorius Debate

The most concrete update came from Sartorius reporting Q3 2026 revenue of €926.3 million and net income of €66.1 million, with net margin rising from 5.2% to 7.1% versus Q3 2025. That shift in profitability leaned toward the bullish story that imagined margin expansion. Tariff and cost concerns in the cautious case were not disproven, so the evidence cut both ways.

The hinge assumption here was margin progress. For any other stock built on a similar thesis, track whether net margin and absolute profit both move toward the forecast rather than just watching headline revenue or the share price.

What Sartorius Is Asking You To Believe Now

Today Sartorius changes hands at €290, and the key question is whether sentiment has moved faster than operations. Revenue in Q3 2026 reached €926.3 million with net income of €66.1 million, and net margin at 7.1% compared with 5.2% a year earlier.

The share price now rests on how durable that profitability shift proves to be. The valuation CTA can help you test how much of the current tag assumes margins will remain close to that higher level.

The return is settled. The valuation question is not. Pinpoint what our model says Sartorius is worth.

Another Bet Beside Sartorius

If Sartorius puts bioprocessing in view, your mind may jump to therapies themselves. That is only half the picture.

Drug developers still need a steady flow of new medicines to justify all that manufacturing capacity. One large healthcare group is pushing deeper into cancer, immunology and brain disorders.

If that pipeline keeps feeding new launches, the demand pattern around Sartorius could look very different to what its own orders alone reveal.

data.title: Orkla India Limited Just Recorded A 9.8% EPS Beat: Here's What Analysts Are Forecasting Next
data.description:
As you might know, Orkla India Limited (NSE:ORKLAINDIA) just kicked off its latest second-quarter results with some very strong numbers. The company beat expectations with revenues of ₹7.8b arriving 6.6% ahead of forecasts. Statutory earnings per share (EPS) were ₹6.70, 9.8% ahead of estimates. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. With this in mind, we've gathered the latest statutory forecasts to see what the analysts are expecting for next year.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Following the latest results, Orkla India's six analysts are now forecasting revenues of ₹27.8b in 2027. This would be a reasonable 2.6% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Per-share earnings are expected to accumulate 5.1% to ₹23.71. In the lead-up to this report, the analysts had been modelling revenues of ₹27.8b and earnings per share (EPS) of ₹23.71 in 2027. So it's pretty clear that, although the analysts have updated their estimates, there's been no major change in expectations for the business following the latest results.

View our latest analysis for Orkla India

It will come as no surprise then, to learn that the consensus price target is largely unchanged at ₹717. That's not the only conclusion we can draw from this data however, as some investors also like to consider the spread in estimates when evaluating analyst price targets. Currently, the most bullish analyst values Orkla India at ₹770 per share, while the most bearish prices it at ₹650. This is a very narrow spread of estimates, implying either that Orkla India is an easy company to value, or - more likely - the analysts are relying heavily on some key assumptions.

Taking a look at the bigger picture now, one of the ways we can understand these forecasts is to see how they compare to both past performance and industry growth estimates. It's pretty clear that there is an expectation that Orkla India's revenue growth will slow down substantially, with revenues to the end of 2027 expected to display 5.3% growth on an annualised basis. This is compared to a historical growth rate of 10% over the past year. By way of comparison, the other companies in this industry with analyst coverage are forecast to grow their revenue at 11% per year. So it's pretty clear that, while revenue growth is expected to slow down, the wider industry is also expected to grow faster than Orkla India.

The Bottom Line

The most important thing to take away is that there's been no major change in sentiment, with the analysts reconfirming that the business is performing in line with their previous earnings per share estimates. On the plus side, there were no major changes to revenue estimates; although forecasts imply they will perform worse than the wider industry. There was no real change to the consensus price target, suggesting that the intrinsic value of the business has not undergone any major changes with the latest estimates.

Keeping that in mind, we still think that the longer term trajectory of the business is much more important for investors to consider. At Simply Wall St, we have a full range of analyst estimates for Orkla India going out to 2029, and you can see them free on our platform here..

data.title: Varroc Engineering Limited Earnings Missed Analyst Estimates: Here's What Analysts Are Forecasting Now

Yet prior to the latest earnings, the analysts had been anticipated revenues of ₹106.6b and earnings per share (EPS) of ₹25.79 in 2027. So it looks like there's been no major change in sentiment following the latest results, although the analysts have made a modest lift to to revenue forecasts.

Even though revenue forecasts increased, the consensus price target 12% to ₹764, perhaps suggesting thatthe analysts have become more pessimistic about the lack of earnings growth. McCormick (MKC)

data.title: What Greggs Doubters Overlooked
data.description:
Greggs has not just been opening more shops and consulting on factory closures. It has been reshaping how and where it serves food on the go. Holding Greggs over the past year would have returned 56.9%, including dividends. If you had put money to work before that run, you would have been weighing bullish expansion plans against worries about UK quick-service saturation. What exactly did buyers think they were seeing that justified that call?

Greggs has already moved. See which of 15 high quality undervalued stocks still trade below our estimates.

The Two Greggs Stories Investors Had To Price In

The shares cost £15.76 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Greggs then had to choose which story felt more convincing.

The bullish narrative pointed to a Fair Value of £20.66, a notional price level implied if expansion and digital ordering played out as hoped. That view leaned on Greggs growing revenue through more drive-thrus, retail parks and digital channels, supported by supply chain investments and a focus on value.

The cautious camp worked off a Fair Value of £13.3, a hypothetical price if risks dominated. This side focused on UK quick-service saturation, stricter regulation and rising costs, which could pressure profit margins and limit the benefit of new locations.

What The Results Changed For The Greggs Debate

The most concrete update came from Greggs reporting H1 2026 revenue of £1,101.5m and net income of £56.2m, with net margin at 5.1% versus 4.5% a year earlier. That backed the optimistic case that supply chain spending and new channels could support both sales and profitability. Factory closure plans and 740 proposed redundancies cut the other way, so the evidence still landed mixed.

The practical takeaway is simple. When a thesis leans on efficiency and format expansion, track margin percentage and shop count in each set of results to see if that story is actually turning into cash profit.

What Greggs' Run Up To £23.4 Already Assumes

Greggs now trades at £23.4, and the selected Narrative’s Fair Value sits below that level. The argument is not that the business is broken. It is that the current tag already bakes in clean supply chain execution and strong cash generation translating into generous capital returns.

Anyone paying today is effectively assuming multichannel growth, logistics projects and factory closures slot into place without hurting service or long term earnings. The question is how that assumption holds up if the supply chain programme or future cash return decisions play out differently from what buyers are now implying.

"The main thing that has to go right is execution on supply chain restructuring and new logistics capacity so that factory closures, Derby and Kettering costs and automation projects deliver the targeted returns without disrupting service. The current valuation implies a share price that already prices in continued market share gains, robust free cash generation and further capital returns, which leaves limited room for disappointment if growth, cost savings or returns slow."
